utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom. And good morning to everyone again. I briefly deal with two matters. The first -- both dealing with the testimony of Milenko Jevdjevic. The first one. On the 23rd of February of this year, during the testimony of the said witness, the Prosecution noted that the English translation of Exhibit P7059 was incomplete. This can be found at transcript page 32095. And on 25th of February, the Prosecution informed chamber via an e-mail that a revised translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0204-2643-ET and the Registry is hereby instructed to replace the existing translation with the revised one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Krcmar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Lukic will now continue his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before I continue, I would just offer, since I forgot to offer into evidence, two documents we discussed on Thursday. It's 1D5364, to be MFI'd, since there is no translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, 1D5364 receives number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number would be D919.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D919 is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And another one is 1D5367, also to be MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number would be D920.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D920 is marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krcmar, the Chamber has heard evidence stating that there were members of the Muslim and Croat peoples in the ranks of the VRS. Do you know whether there were any prisoners, Muslims and Croats, people taken prisoner by the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just like members of the VRS were taken prisoner, Croats and Muslims were taken prisoner by their police too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was your knowledge? How were they treated in the prisons of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina or the camps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when I spoke to them during the exchanges, the information I received was that they fared worse than Serb prisoners in these prisons and camps precisely because they belonged to the Muslim or Croat peoples. That is to say, they were beaten. There were a lot of beatings. They were treated inhumanely. Although treatment of Serbs was not correct either, but they had special treatment in prisons.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there any Muslims or Serbs who had been taken prisoner and who did not want to be exchanged, and if you could explain that briefly?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for Serbs who were taken prisoner and were in Muslim prisons, they all expected the day of exchange. However, as far as Muslims in Serb prisons are concerned, there are cases when they did not want to be exchanged precisely because of that explanation, that they would be mobilised again and that they would have to fight a war again. They asked for contact with the International Red Cross and they asked to go to third countries. We established these contacts for them, but, nevertheless, we had to take them to the line of exchange so that they could state their views before the other side, namely, that they did not wish to go to the other side, so that they could go to third countries, and they could, this way, provide scope for us for an unhindered exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, for pages now, this happened in general, there, et cetera, without any verifiable facts. Just for you to know that, of course, this Chamber very much appreciates if it hears detailed facts such as where this happened, how this happened, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krcmar, you heard what the Judge is interested in.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you have --

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand, I understand. The exchanges that took place between the 1st Krajina Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska and the 5th Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina from Bihac, we had quite a few situations when people did not cross over to the side of the 5th Corps. As for names, I really cannot go into that now because over 10.000 names were dealt with. People who were exchanged on both sides. I simply cannot remember all of these names, but there were cases like this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now that you're talking about that area, Bihac and the 5th Corps, do you know anything about exchanges of prisoners that happened between the Muslim-protected factions, that is to say, the army that was in Western Bosnia, the Autonomous Region of Western Bosnia, and the 5th Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I attended several meetings where missing persons from both sides were discussed. When I say "from both sides," I mean the 5th Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Army of the Autonomous Region of Western Bosnia. That is to say, the two Muslim armies. It was very hard to establish co-operation between those two warring parties. The International Committee of the Red Cross acted as an intermediary and even asked us to help bring these two sides to the negotiating table. Although we managed to organise joint meetings, the process of talks was rather painstaking and rather difficult precisely between these two warring parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who addressed you on behalf of the international community asking to you mediate in these negotiations?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, the ICRC and the representatives of the UN at the time, that is to say, the representative was, I think, Ivan Betir [phoen]. I think that was the name. After the war, that gentleman remained in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and he was an officer in the IPTF.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We talked about registering mortal remains in morgues. During the course of your work, did you come across any official information as to how many Muslims from Srebrenica went missing in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not come across such information at all because the official lists of missing persons, both in Bosnia-Herzegovina and in Srebrenica, there actually is no such thing. All of that is within the sphere of guess-work, day-to-day politics, or presenting the kind of information that may suit someone at some point in time. So, as I've already said in my statement, right now in Bosnia-Herzegovina, 8- to 13.000 missing persons is the figure that is being bandied about in Bosnia-Herzegovina now, which really cannot be serious.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P4008, please, could we have that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you something about this document once we have it on our screens. During proofing, I showed you this document; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know what this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is your understanding of this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document shows that the state Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners of War headed by Dragan Bulajic reached an agreement with the Muslim side about the exchange of prisoners of war. What I do not see here is that the military commission negotiated about the exchange because the military commission did not have the mandate to talk about exchanges with the other side when it is civilians that are being referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us please take a look at the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the president of the state commission, Dragan Bulajic, shall be allowed to transfer all prisoners from our prisons to Kula prison in the area of Sarajevo-Romanija Corps in order to have the exchange conducted simultaneously on the 5th of October, 1994, and the 11th of October, 1994. Why, then, do we see General Tolimir's signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Main Staff co-ordinated the issue of POWs and exchanges. As far as I can see, this has to do with an exchange of POWs where there were civilians involved too. So if they were in prisons of the corps, it is logical that the Main Staff had to be involved in such exchanges or in the release of prisoners from prisons that were in the area of responsibility of the corps. If they were really prisoners in prison. I repeat once again: This is an exchange that was agreed upon by the civilian commission, and probably before that, there was some kind of agreement reached at the level of the civilian commission and the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. We did not have the mandate or right to discuss anything with regard to civilians on either side. These were clear instructions that we had from the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of preparations were supposed to be carried out at the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to have an exchange of POWs, because there were war operations still going on, the Main Staff or the corps command had to make a decision on a cease-fire. So such an activity could not be carried out without the agreement of the Main Staff, actually without a cessation of combat operations. The civilian commission did not have a mechanism or the mandate to stop combat operations because the army was not under its authority. Also there were other cases when civilians would cross from one side to the other. But again, I repeat, that is the Main Staff that had to give their agreement so that combat operations would be stopped on either side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we briefly just go back to the video now. I think is in indispensable for the sake of context for us to see two other clips. D917 MFI, that's what we're going to see on our screens now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's look at 31 minutes, 18 seconds to 31 minutes, 37 seconds, and then I'll have a question for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know any of the Serbian soldiers who were killed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know all the three who were first taken prisoners and then killed on the 21st of September, 1992. It happened between Maglaj Teslic and Tesanj at the feature known as Crni Vrh. We can see a Mujahedin here holding a severed Serbian head in his hand. His name is Nenad Petkovic. His father's name was Tomislav. All the three bodies were received beheaded. To this very day the heads have not been found. All the families have been insisting and calling every day in order to have heads found. I would like to say something else but the case of Nenad Petkovic. We can see his severed head in the video-clip. When the bodies were buried, they would not tell his mother that the body was without a head. Sometime after the war, on the way to Belgrade in Serbia, she was reading a Serbian magazine and she saw her son's head being held by Mujahedin and she died after that. Let me also say that the other two men are Djuric and Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were those photos published in the media already during the war? When were those photos obtained?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps a couple months after those events, during combat a soldier of the BiH army was killed. He was a Mujahedin. Around his neck a camera was found. The film in the camera was developed and that's how these photos and some other photos were obtained. These photos were publicised and -- and people felt hatred. They wanted to revenge, to retaliate, for the way the prisoners of war were treated. Bearing in mind that that was done by the BiH army and its members who hailed from other states rather than from Bosnian-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now just briefly let me show you something else. And that will bring us to the end of the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1 hour, 37 minutes, 14 seconds is the beginning, to 1 hour 37 minutes, 48 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "The head was severed at the third cervical vertebrae which is destroyed at that place, showing that the neck was cut by a blow from the blade of a sharp mechanical object."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was doing the post-mortem of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The pathologist was Zoran Stankovic, a forensic expert affiliated with the Military Medical Academy in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did this happen and where?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: These bodies were found in Podrinje in the place called Skelani. Forty locals of -- of Skelani were skilled on the 16th of January, 1993, and their heads were severed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when was the post-mortem done?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately after the people were killed. The Muslim forces attacked Serbian villages, killed people, and then withdrew. They left the bodies behind. The bodies were then discovered, and then a judiciary order was issued, post-mortems were carried out, and this was taken from the archives of the MUP of Serbia. That was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the general public abreast of this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The general public followed all of those events. And all one can feel when looking at these scenes is horror, just as we are horrified today when we are looking at things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can remove that from the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you have your statement before you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be provided with his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of your testimony, Judge Orie said that we should provide an explanation of the annexes at the end of your statement, those that we tendered as associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to call up 1D05233.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krcmar, could you tell us where this image from and what does it represent?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an excerpt from the site entitled: "The missing in Republika Srpska." This is an electronic map of Bosnia-Herzegovina which depicts all the municipalities in Bosnia-Herzegovina where burial sites of the Serbian people were found and all the other exhumations that was carried out by the office of the missing persons in Republika Srpska. In these municipalities, if we were to open each and every one of them, we would arrive at 1400 locations of individual and mass graves where a total of 4100 missing persons were found. Out of them we identified about 3500 as I have stated in my statement. And if we look at Republika Srpska, you will see that there are municipalities there where the bodies of Serb soldiers have been exhumed. These municipalities represent the places where our commission carried out the exhumation of Muslims and Croats that we later handed over to the commission of the federation. If we knew that there were burial sites, we carried out -- carried out exhumations of all the bodies that were found there, not only the bodies of Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, what we see on the screen, is it supposed to be an earlier version of the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question, Your Honour, I'm not sure if I understood the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see the left side it's in B/C/S. The right side is in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's already on the site in both languages. This is a copy from the site since we cannot have the site in the evidence. So we copied several pages from that site, and I will ask this gentleman about the site as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So these are not supposed to be a translation of the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is translation already on that site --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The right side is not a translation of the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, but is already on the site. So you just click the button and you change the language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you should clarify. It is not a translation prepared by CLSS. It is an English version which is found on the same web site as where the -- the Serbian version is found. And that means about accuracy, we do not know yet. It may be very accurate. But that is what it is but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But for sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They are not the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: They are not the same. They are different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you look and it doesn't take you a lot of time to see on the right on the English version there are at the left bottom, there are two red dots, whereas in the original there are four. So, therefore, the accuracy of it seems not yet to be fully established.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you know, the sites are alive so they are refreshed over time. So probably the B/C/S version is refreshed faster than English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whatever explanation you have for it, it may be clear that on first sight that at least - explained by whatever - there are differences between the left one, that is the B/C/S one, and the right one which is the English one. Mr. Traldi, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to briefly ask that the Defence make clear which they intend to rely upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will definitely rely on B/C/S version. And, if necessary, we will add -- although we can explain those differences as well. I think that it's easy, since those places are municipalities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Don't testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Don't testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, of course, my -- I would say it's not the first time I put the question. What is here in dispute, that there were -- apparently this is to show that there were many graves, including mass graves, as you said, and it is explained in paragraph 48. This apparently is image 1-1, which, as you say, of what the witness said, that there are 1400 graves with -- in a total -- a total of 4100 bodies were found. I don't know whether that's dispute about that or -- perhaps not the exact number but in general terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Right. In general terms there is no dispute regarding numbers. Of course, we're happy to speak with the Defence and see if it's possible to come a more specific agreement as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krcmar, you can see the difference on the screen. In B/C/S, we can see four red dots, and in the English version, we can see only two. Where are the municipalities, do they have anything to do with the map?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to explain. I am the creator of this web site. My intention was to show the suffering of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina. If you will allow me, the institutions of Bosnia-Herzegovina, when they mounted an exhibition, they excluded all Serbian burial sites. That's why we created this site. There are no misunderstandings here. Let me just say that on the left-hand side we can see the municipalities of Zadar, Pakrac, and Split. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. And Slavonski Brod.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and Slavonski Brod. These municipalities are not in Bosnia-Herzegovina. They are in the Republic of Croatia. We found some Serbs who were missing from the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina there. So we can easily ignore these municipalities because they are not on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. What we can ignore and what we cannot ignore is, first of all, for the Chamber to make up. Mr. Lukic, it is not only that text. There are really differences between the two. For example, if you look at approximately at the middle of the left side, in the B/C/S version I see two blue dots. On the other version, I see only one blue dot. So, therefore, there are differences, there are -- it -- they're just not the same. And if you say, Well, we can explain that, well, first of all, why -- in general there is no dispute about it, that there were many mass graves -- many graves including graves containing many bodies. Therefore, the one is not the same as the other. And whether it can be explained or not, every exhibit should be accompanied by a translation, a reliable translation, accurate translation. Which of the two do you take as your starting point? Do you start with the English, then we need a better version of the B/C/S. If you start with a B/C/S version, then we need a better one in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We start with B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: B/C/S. Okay. Then for the time being, we do not have an accurate English version of this document, although, let's be fair as well, it seems that most of the dots are the same, but there are many differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There are some differences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Many, many differences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll do our best to correct the differences, Your Honours. So this is then -- just use English translation to help Your Honours to understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you agree with the Prosecution on what it more or less depicts and the Prosecution seems to be ready do that, then that saves you a lot of work. Please proceed. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I can say we're in continuing discussions with the Defence about demographic evidence and numbers of dots.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll wait for the outcome of that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can have 1D05234, please. Again, to be on the safe side, I will rely on the B/C/S version. I don't know how it stands now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krcmar, let me ask you this: How often is this site refreshed and updated? Has it been updated recently? Have you had any problems with updating the site?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the B/C/S version is concerned, it is accurate and correct. The English version takes a bit more time because some technical issues have to be resolved and a translator has to be hired to do that. We rely on the B/C/S version because we're talking about the area of former -- of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the former Yugoslavia, and most of the interested parties come from there. This is a technical issue because there's a discrepancy between the English version and the B/C/S version, but there's nothing wrong with the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What do we have before us on the screen? Just briefly.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we click on one of the municipalities from the previous map, this time we are dealing with Sarajevo, the municipality Centar, the centre, and it shows how many mass graves were found there. Could we zoom in a bit so that I can comment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Since the English version is not identical with the B/C/S, we can remove the English one, because the last paragraph, the fourth bullet point is much longer in B/C/S than in English. So if that can be enlarged, the witness can easily read it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is precisely what we see here, municipality of Sarajevo, Centar. Let me sate that Sarajevo consists of ten municipalities. Here we see that in the municipality of Centar, four mass graves were found. The first one is 28 bodies. The other one is 36 bodies. The third one is 16 bodies. And over here we have three other bodies from the Lav mass grave. Also we can open this version where we see the individual graves; that is to say, there is this distinction between individual graves and mass graves. This time we tried to show mass graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D05235, could we please see that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is this before us?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before us is the process of exhumation of one of these four mass graves that were shown. This is the so-called Lav mass grave where 36 bodies were exhumed. The Lav mass grave is in the very centre of Sarajevo below the Kosevo hospital. These photographs show how the exhumation took place. There are nine photographs. And on the right-hand side, we have a PDF document that is a list of the bodies that were identified from that mass grave and then there are other bodies that were not identified and they were marked by an NN.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please explain what you mean by on the right-hand side we see a list of victims? Perhaps if you click on the screen, then you will find it, but I don't see a list. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As we continue, we will see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I say what I wanted to say. Maybe we should remove the English because again they're not identical, these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, any dispute, Mr. Traldi, about an exhumation of the number of 36 bodies of Serb -- of Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it best be treated as part of our ongoing discussions with the Defence. Specific numbers remain sort of a matter of communication between the parties. Certainly no dispute that there are mass graves in the Sarajevo area or that there's one at Lav.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will skip now, since there are only enlarged photographs we see on this one, from 1D05236 up to 1D05243. And then I would go to 1D05244.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe it's easier for you on the screen. I hope that this translation is the same. What is this before us, Mr. Krcmar?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely what I said a moment ago. If we open the PDF document, we will see the list of all the bodies that were found. If they were identified, then we have the names and surnames of the identified persons and their details. If they are NN, then they remain there as unidentified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lukic, there was a similar list attached to the statement of the witness, but that one is not identical to what we see on our screen, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not. That's what we discovered during our preparations. Because this one is -- from the computer. Has not been uploaded into the -- on the web site yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Web site is slower process, especially English part of the web site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, do you want to rely on the one that we have on the screen now or -- because we have as an associated exhibit, of course, we have what seems to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would rather rely on this one and it can be replaced which is in the statement since it's a more recent one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The one on the screen is more recent?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, one in the statement is more recent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The one in the statement is more recent, yes. It at least gives more details about the -- especially about the unknown deceased persons, including where they are found in the ICMP list, et cetera. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krcmar, what do you know about the exhumations themselves? What is your role?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Could you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What do you know about exhumations in the field? What is your role?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1996, I have been attending exhumations. Out of these 1400 locations, I have dealt with over 80 per cent of them. My role in the quest for missing persons starts with the initial reporting of a missing person either by the family or unit; setting up a database; seeking information on the ground; locating graves, mass graves, individual graves; marking graves; familiarizing the judiciaries in charge of the locations found; and submitting requests to these institutions for carrying out exhumations. I took part the exhumations themselves, then also the transportation of bodies, keeping bodies, post-mortems, taking part in forensic post-mortems. Then identification, inviting families to these identifications, communicating results, and finally handing over the bodies for burial to the families. So that is a complete process, from beginning to end.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask now to have D91 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Mr. Lukic, what do you intend to do? You say you would rely on the more recent one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just want to place this gentleman's statement on the screen and that page from his statement. Not this 1D exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but they are all mentioned as -- they are mentioned in the statement of the witness and we find the pictures of the newer -- do you want to upload them into e-court so that we have not the one as we find it on our screen, but we have the one which is attached to the witness's evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you still have to upload, then, the newer versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I'm somewhat surprised because the statement was taken in July 2014, that's eight months ago, and now eight months later you still come with what seems to be an older version, which would mean prior to July 2014. I don't know when you uploaded it. I don't know what you -- where you got it from, but for eight months you are at least aware that there's a newer one with more information, which is not in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I -- we tried to download from the site what we found on the site, but in the statement, that's true, are newer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you're supposed to copy this from the statement, scan it, copy it, upload it into e-court so that at least we have the same versions in e-court as we find them as attached to the statement of the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need D916 on our screens. And we need page 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Lav grave is in front of us now. First of all, where were these people found? What kind of grave is this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since we've skipped these photographs, I need to explain. These bodies were found 4 metres away from the road, underneath the Kosevo hospital, deep down, after the bodies that were later buried. Actually, over the Lav grave, newborn children were buried. So we had quite a few problems in order to carry out this exhumation; namely that we could remove the newborns in order to reach this grave. There were terrible obstructions from the federal commission and they did not allow the removal of these bodies. So the grave containing 36 bodies was masked with the bodies of newborn babies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this table, the third group horizontally from the bottom, the first column, it says Fadil Kujovic. In your view, what would his ethnicity be?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a Muslim. We identified that body, and we handed it over to the family so that they could bury him. The identification took place in 2012, as far as I can see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Samir Hasanbegovic is next to him?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Samir Hasanbegovic who was born in 1968, 1968. He is also a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in line 3, just one line up, we see Djelal Hodzic. That's what's written there.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Djelal Hodzic, born in 1956, is also a Muslim. These bodies were identified considerably earlier and handed over to Sejo Koso, a member of the exchanges commission, and then he handed the bodies over to the families for burial.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These three Muslims, were they found together with the Serbs who were buried, as you say, very deep, 4 metres deep?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were found with the Serbs. I did not say that it was 4 metres deep. I said that it was 4 metres away from the road. The depth was 2 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the course of your work, did you find out how come these three bodies of deceased Muslims were buried there? Do you know how they lost their lives?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since this is Sarajevo, the centre of town, the Serb army and Serbs could not be in Sarajevo at the time. That is to say, this was directly under the control of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. How they died, we don't know. Just like we don't know how come these Serbs of ours were killed too. Probably somebody tried to conceal a crime and bury them together with Serbs. I would just like to add one more thing. What happened --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you do so, you say you don't know how they died. Have any post-mortems been conducted on these bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, all the bodies that were exhumed, all 4.100 were dealt with forensically -- well, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm talking about these. It says 36. I think I find 39 boxes in the scheme, but were post-mortems conducted on those persons found here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right, 39. And now I'm going to explain the 39. Yes, all of them were dealt with forensically, but a forensic medical expert can testify about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But do you know the outcome of it? I mean, I'm not asking for any details, but in your work, did you ever find that they were killed, for example, by shot wounds or that they were killed by strangling? I mean, sometimes even without knowing the details of the forensic expert conclusions, you sometimes can read what the final conclusion is. Are you aware of the conclusion in relation to these persons in general and, more specifically, about the three Muslims found among them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I know that they suffered a forceable death, a violent death. I suppose that forensic experts could tell you more about the nature of their wounds. I can't talk about that. I only know that they died a violent death.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's break time anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can inform that I will use less time than I announced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And how much time --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 10, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 10, 15 minutes left. Then we'll take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes, and you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness to come in, I'll deal with the second remaining issue related to the testimony of Milenko Jevdjevic. P7136 was marked for identification on the 23rd of February of this year, during the testimony of Jevdjevic, pending a translation. This can be found at transcript page 32082. On the 25th of February, the Prosecution informed the Chamber via an e-mail that a translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID number 0320-4600-ET. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to attach the translation and admits into evidence P7136 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you're ready, you're invited to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krcmar, we're coming to the end of this examination. I'm going to ask you how many Serbs have been exhumed in Sarajevo so far?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: A total of 471 bodies have been exhumed so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was anybody held accountable, was anybody convicted for crimes against the Serbs in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, nobody has been held accountable for the 471 bodies that I have just mentioned. There was a trial in respect of a group of perpetrators or a group of victims, but in that case, the person was found to be unfit for trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It hasn't been recorded. What burial site was that about?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the burial site called Kazani, a pit above Sarajevo into which the bodies of the Serbs were thrown.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since we have mentioned that burial site, what has happened to it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That grave, in the course of 1993 and 1994, was moved from that location. The bodies were moved to Sarajevo, and they were buried in the Kosevo football pitch in Sarajevo. A total of 27 bodies were buried there. There was 27 markings during the exhumation, 26 bodies were buried, and the last -- one of the last markings, actually, marked the bones of an animal, of a dog.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said the auxiliary Kosevo football pitch; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a football pitch in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are we talking football?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, football. Football.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now let's move to Bihac. Only in our minds, of course. Is there a barracks in Bihac?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Its name is Adil Beslic. It used to be called the Luka barracks during the war. Now it's the barracks of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the war, who was billeted there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 5th Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was billeted there during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How is your work connected to the barracks?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that in the course of 1994 and in 1995, 21 Serbian prisoners were held there. We were involved in negotiations to set those people free. Unfortunately, they never came out alive. All the 21 prisoners were killed in the barracks. In the course of 1996, we received six bodies in exchange from that barracks and we identified them. On several occasions, we tried to carry out an exhumation, and then in the year 2000, in that same barracks where the forces of the BiH are now billeted, we found a mass grave containing eight bodies of the 21. They were exhumed, identified, and their bodies were handed over to their families. In that barracks, there are still the bodies of seven people. We obtained that information owing to the fact that we actually bought the information. Our informer had told us about the remaining seven bodies, and that the former commander who was billeted in the barracks as well as the current commanders of the barracks should be aware of their whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who were members of the command during the war?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war, one of the commanders of the barracks for logistics was Major Mujo Begic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now what is his position?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mujo Begic has obtained a doctoral degree, his topic was war crime, and he is the head of the office of the Institute for Missing Persons of Bosnia-Herzegovina headquartered in Bihac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that he was the head of the Bihac office?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that what's I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many offices does the institute of Bosnia-Herzegovina currently have?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Currently they are there 16 offices of the institute located around Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since the federal offices have been established, how many Serbs have these 16 offices located over the past six years?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thirteen offices are on the Bosnia-Herzegovina Federation side, and those 13 offices have located only three Serb bodies. Two in Zavidovici and one in the territory of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krcmar, thank you. This is all that we had prepared for you.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Traldi, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krcmar, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. You find Mr. Traldi to your right. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, you testified in the Delic case; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you gave statements to the OTP in 2005 and 2007, as you've discussed earlier; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not received interpretation. No interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your question, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And your testimony in the Delic case, as well as the statements you gave in 2005 and 2007, that was truthful evidence you were providing; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you gave an interview to the OTP in 2010 as well; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And did you tell the truth on that occasion too?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you mention you're head of the Department for Tracing Missing Persons in the State Centre for War Crimes Research. That's obviously the Republika Srpska Centre for Tracing Missing Persons; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we were talking at cross-purposes. I was the head of a team of the government of Republika Srpska for tracing missing persons up to 2012. In 2012, the republican centre and the operative were merged into one institution and now it's called Republican Centre for the Research of War Crimes and Tracing Missing Persons. I am currently the chief of the Department for Tracing Missing Persons. I'm not the head of the entire centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, your work up to 2012 had been with the Republika Srpska government; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1996 until this very day, I have been working for the government of Republika Srpska. But the names of the institution has changed. It was the institute, the commission, the office, the operative, and now it is the republican centre. However, my job has remained the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in that job, it's fair to say your work focuses largely on cases involving missing Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Amongst other things. However, in my work, as I've already told you, we have also traced over 300 missing Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now you mentioned the number of 4100 people on direct examination that were reflected on the web site. Are the 300 Muslims and Croats you just mentioned included in those 4100 or additional to it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The site comprises only those persons who were reported to us as missing. In this case, the 300 people have never been reported to us. We found them, exhumed them, and we handed them over to the federal commission or directly to their families, depending on the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm aware we're talking about your area of professional expertise, but I'd just ask you to try to provide a focused answer to the questions that I'm asking you. And, in this case, I take it, that those 300 people are not part of the 4.100 you mentioned earlier; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. With them, it would be over 4100, so they would be on top of the figure. You are right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now while your work primarily relates to missing Serbs, you co-operate with institutions that are looking for missing Muslims as well, you go to meetings together, talk to them about your work; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was up to 2008. That's how things were up to then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in the course of doing so, you receive information about missing Muslims, missing Croats, and also you learn about crimes that may have been committed that resulted in those people becoming missing; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now I want to turn now two of the terms you discussed on direct examination and try to distinguish very carefully, if you'll assist us. First, the term "cases" that you discussed at some length, that refers to bodies or parts of bodies that have been located but have not yet been identified; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only body parts. Bodies are bodies. In the forensic science there is not a term "case." That term, the term "case" has been established --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to -- I'd asked a very specific question and I understood you to answer that the term "cases" refers to body parts; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the term "missing persons," on the other hand, refers to persons who have been reported as missing and whose remains have not yet been identified; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, everybody who has a name. The first and the last names.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the parts of bodies that comprise cases as a general rule, have been exhumed years after the war, sometimes 20 or more years after they'd been killed; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ever since 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And many of them are partial because the bodies were buried in mass graves and often reburied, moved to other locations or -- sorry, excavated, moved to other locations and reburied, in that order, of course, using heavy machinery of the sort that might disturb the integrity of a given set of remains; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were cases like that. Bodies were, indeed, moved into secondary graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you're aware that, for instance, the ICMP maintains a very large database of genetic samples so as to compare remains which are located and tested to about 150.000 samples of the DNA of relatives of people who have been reported as missing; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, whenever families provided blood for DNA testing, ICMP has the results. But there were also cases of families refusing to provide a sample and that's where the ICMP has a problem. There are also cases where all the families went missing or there's not a very close family member to provide a blood sample.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you estimated on Thursday that there about 2.500 bodies in morgues pending identification. And you'd agree with me that separate from those bodies still in the morgue, 20 years after the conflict, there are 7.000 or more people, based on publicly available information, who have been reported missing and whose remains have not yet been identified; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the case. We cannot agree about that. We cannot agree that there 7.000 cases pending. There is no record of missing persons in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that's why the figure is being manipulated and ranges from 8.000 to 13.000. I'm not going to state and favour any of these figures because there is not a clear record. The record hasn't been established so it is really not serious to come up with any figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to leave that topic for the moment and I'm going to turn now to your evidence about the 1st Krajina Corps Exchange Commission which you discussed in your statement and very briefly during direct examination. Now, you mentioned that each of the VRS corps had its own exchange commission. Did those exchange commissions all function similarly within their areas of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were six commissions. They operated based on the instructions received from the corps commands and the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. And then depending on the situation of the commission or the corps and the number of losses, they did what they were supposed to do, but I -- we cannot say that they functioned in the same way because the issues that they dealt with and the circumstances were different.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I understand they wouldn't have faced exactly the same issues or circumstances. But they functioned under similar regulations, similar orders, addressing similar types of problems; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now you say you began serving as a member of the commission in 1993. Who was your immediate superior when you were a member of the commission?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedeljko Savic, the president of the commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And who was his superior?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along the hierarchy line of the command, it was the department for morale, guidance, and religious issues, the commission was under its authority, and the person in charge was Colonel Jovo Blazanovic, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you discuss -- you provide evidence about prisoners and about the activities of the exchange commission. Should we understand your evidence about prisoners and about the activities of the exchange commission to refer to the time-period when you served as a member of the exchange commission?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can say from April 1993 until April 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you discuss both civilian and military exchange commissions in your statement. The military exchange commissions had close co-operation with the civilian exchange commissions; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We co-operated closely with the civilian commission for the exchange but that went through the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska and the corps commands. We couldn't do anything without their instruction or if information was not provided to us either by a corps command or the Main Staff. It all depended on the problem and its gravity.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And at times, with the consent, of course, and on the order of your superior commands, you would co-operate with the civilian commission in the implementation of a particular exchange; right? A particular exchange might involve organising efforts and representatives of both the military exchange commission and the civilian exchange commission.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand you. Did you mention the Supreme Command? Did you have in mind the Main Staff or who did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When I referred to your superior commands, I was referring to the corps command and the Main Staff as you had just referred to, sir.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now I understand. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Before I do, would you mind answering the question that I had asked. And I can repeat it, if that would assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps that would be good.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So with the consent and on the order of your superior commands, which refers to the corps command and the Main Staff, you would co-operate with the civilian commission in the implementation of particular exchanges; right? A particular exchange might involve organising efforts by and representatives of both the military exchange commission and the civilian exchange commission.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we worked exclusively on the instructions of the Main Staff and the corps commands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's still not an answer to the question. The question was whether on particular exchanges the civilian commission and the military commission would have a joint effort in organising such exchanges. That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't have any joint exchanges. If a civilian commission agreed the exchange, it would be in charge of its implementation. And if, on the other hand, it was a military commission who agreed an exchange, it would also implement it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let me perhaps see if can I ask in a very focused way. There were times, weren't there, when, at a particular time in a particular place, the civilian exchange commission and the military exchange commission both brought people to that place to be exchanged, and people were received from the Muslim side in the course of being exchanged; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But everybody brought people in within the domain of their own agreement and handed them over.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And among the members of the civilian exchange commission -- I'm speaking now of the Republika Srpska level civilian exchange commission at the time you served on the 1st Krajina Corps commission, so April 1993 through the end of the war. During that period, there were VRS officers who served on the civilian exchange commission; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the commission of the 1st Krajina Corps, nobody worked in the civilian commission. Nobody from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm going to sorry to interrupt and just clarify. You referred to a man named Dragan Bulajic in your statement. That's Captain Dragan Bulajic; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what rank Mr. Bulajic held. He was on the civilian commission, not the military commission, and he had no authority with regard to resolving the question of POWs. He had nothing to do with the Main Staff and our military commissions. So he was appointed by the president of the republic, not the Main Staff, not the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also he did not report to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm certainly not -- I didn't ask whether he reported to you. I didn't ask who appointed him. All I asked is: Dragan Bulajic was a VRS officer; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Dragan Bulajic was not a soldier of the Army of Republika Srpska, the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you know what job he held in 1992 before he became president of the civilian exchange commission?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's look at a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 08207.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a document sent by the Sokolac municipality's POW exchange committee. It's dated the 9th of November, 1992, and it's addressed to the Army of Republika Srpska, Lukavica committee for exchange and freeing of POWs. Attention: President Dragan Bulajic. Now, the Army of Republika Srpska exchange committee based at Lukavica was, of course, the SRK's exchange commission; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, did you say SRK?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I did and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're translated as RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that's a very important distinction. Thank you very much, Your Honour. I'll reask.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska exchange committee based at Lukavica was the exchange commission of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that's where the headquarters were of the military commission of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps at Lukavica and Dragan Bulajic had separate office at Lukavica. But this has to do with the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. I can testify here about the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you co-operated with -- your corps' exchange commission co-operated with the other corps' exchange commissions; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In fact, you knew what building Dragan Bulajic's office was in, as you've just testified, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you said that Captain Bulajic had an office at Lukavica, two follow-up questions. First, you're referring to the Lukavica barracks; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the barracks, that's where the military commission was. Maybe I should make a correction. I think that Mr. Dragan Bulajic had an office at Grbavica. I think. I am afraid that I may be making a mistake. But these were two separate offices, not one, which is what you have been alluding to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, what I'm alluding to is what this document clearly says about November 1992. When you say that they had separate offices, you're referring to the period when you were on the exchange commission, 1993 through the end of the war; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but you're asking me something that is outside the authority of my corps and outside the time when I was on the commission for exchanges.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot testify about this because I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, let me be clear on that. Whatever your authority was or the authority of your corps, you're questioned about what you know. If you know anything about it, tell us; if you say, I don't know, tell us as well. But don't tell us that it was beyond your responsibilities and that for that reason you can't give testimony on that. Whatever you know, you're supposed to tell us in response to questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd tender 65 ter 08207.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm a bit hesitant but I would object since this gentleman has no knowledge about this document and has nothing to do with the time-period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, he testified about offices in Lukavica and that Lukavica was barracks different from Grbavica. So therefore the witness did, although not extensively, testify on this document. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document number 08207 receives number P7158.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence from a Main Staff officer named Spiro Pereula. He also served on the civilian exchange commission; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that man.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now returning to Captain Bulajic. He was appointed president of the civilian exchange commission in 1993; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when he was appointed. He was appointed president of the civilian commission, now I don't know exactly -- was it 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, before him, there was a president of the civilian commission named Nenad Vanovac; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not know about the structure of the civilian commission. In 1993, when I arrived, Dragan Bulajic was there. I really don't know --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear the end of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, have you been asked to repeat the end of your answer. The interpreters weren't able to hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all unnecessary microphones please be switched off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know anything about these people. In 1993, when I was appointed to the commission of the 1st Krajina Corps, Dragan Bulajic was also president of the civilian commission. I'm not aware of the structure as it existed before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, it's your evidence that it was the civilian exchange commission that was responsible for exchanging non-Serb civilians who, through that process, were exchanged out of Republika Srpska territory; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assert that the civilian commission did not have the mandate to deal with the military and that it was in charge of civilian affairs, civilian persons and --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to confirm, if you can, the specific proposition that I put to you, that it's your evidence that the civilian exchange commission was responsible for exchanging non-Serb civilians who, through that process, were exchanged out of Republika Srpska territory. Is that your evidence, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in this sense. The civilian commission was in charge of civilians, all Serbs, Croats, Muslims, all the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The people that the civilian commission exchanged with the commission on the Muslim or Croat side, those people left Republika Srpska as a result of the exchanges, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go into the powers of that commission, what they did, how they did that. I can repeat this. I can testify about the military commission, military exchanges. I was not on that other commission. I don't know what people did. I know that --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I put to you that the reason that you are suggesting that you don't know that the civilian exchange commission exchanged civilians who left Republika Srpska as a result, is that you're aware that it's alleged that the civilian exchange commission, in doing so, was -- was part of the process of ethnically cleansing Serb-claimed territory. You're aware of those allegations, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what you are claiming. That is not what I have been claiming.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're aware that since the war, in fact, beginning early in the war, allegations were made that the exchange process was part of the machinery of ethnic cleansing; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Please. There was a process of exchanging POWs that I can testify about here. What you have asked me about is something that I cannot testify about because I did not take part that any such thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, sometimes we -- even without taking part in something, you may have knowledge about it. If you have any knowledge about it, please tell us, irrespective of whether you took part in it. And one of the previous questions that Mr. Traldi put to you is whether the civilians who were exchanged, in the context of that exchange left Republika Srpska. That was a question which has not been answered yet by you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall respond to you, Your Honour. Civilians, as far as I know, were not exchanged. Civilians left voluntarily in organised fashion, either to third countries or the territory of the present-day Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But irrespective now, those who -- no, I leave it to that. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I put to you that Captain Bulajic was the president of an exchange commission, not a people-leaving-voluntarily commission and your testimony in this regard is not credible. Do you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no comment what -- as to what Dragan Bulajic did. But I repeated to you a moment ago what it was that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now to another area of what you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before do you that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you do that, I would kindly ask the witness to explain the word "in organised fashion." You said: "Civilians left voluntarily in organised fashion." Who organised that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can say about Banja Luka because I'm from Banja Luka and I was there at the time. There was an agency that organised departures of persons from Banja Luka. They applied to that agency, and I know that when we, military commissions, negotiated with the other sides, then that time was used for people to take buses and come to the separation line and cross to the other side from there. That is to say, these departures were organised. Now was it for family reunification or something like that, people left in that organised way. They didn't leave out of detention facilities or prisons but they left of their own free will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You didn't quite answer my question. I was asking you who organised that? Because you said in general terms it was -- they left in organised fashion. Now you said: "There was an agency that organised departures of persons from Banja Luka." Which agency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot, I really don't know the exact answer now. There was this agency of the government that had nothing do with the military. This agency that was for the departure of these persons. Now whether some people went to third countries, I know that you could go that way and I know that people could go to the present-day territory of the federation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You said "this agency of the government." Which government?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told you what it is that I know. Really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which government?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is an agency of the government of Republika Srpska that had an agency. Now, did it really belong to the government of Republika Srpska? I know that such an agency did exist, but it was not within the domain of my own work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one follow-up question to you. You said there were no exchanges. People only voluntarily left. One of your answers, and I read it, was, asked about civilian commission and the military commission: "We didn't have any joint exchanges. If a civilian commission agreed exchange, it would be in charge of its implementation. And if, on the other hand, it was a military commission who agreed an exchange, it would also implement it." Which at least suggests that you have the opinion that civilian commission agreed exchanges and not only facilitated voluntary departure. Any comment on what I just read?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do have a comment. As for the Federation, many Serbs from that side came to Republika Srpska voluntarily on buses. Also, on the same day, from Banja Luka, from Republika Srpska, actually, Muslims and Croats would cross over to the other side. Now can we call that an exchange or could we call it a crossing? That is a question of terminology.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The head of the agency in Banja Luka that you referred to a moment, you know that to be Radovan Glogovac, don't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has also received evidence from him. He testified he was appointed to the exchange commission at the suggestion of President Karadzic and of Minister Ostojic. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now to another area. I notice in your statement you claim you were mobilised into the VRS at the beginning of the war. In fact, in May 1992, you became a member of the special unit of the Banja Luka CSB; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was mobilised first into the corps military police. The army, that is, the Army of Republika Srpska. And then I was transferred. My military occupational specialty is that of policeman, so then I was assigned to the civilian police and I spent some time there, I don't know exactly how long, and then I returned to the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to explore that in a little more detail but I want to start with a couple of very focused questions. Who was it, if you recall, that told you you had been assigned to the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. I don't understand the question. Who said what to me? I was called up, and my VES, my military occupational specialty, was that of a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, you said were mobilised into the military and then you were assigned to the civilian police. How was it that you were assigned to the civilian police. How was that communicated to you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably call-up. After all these years, I cannot give an answer. It's been a long time, and I've really been dealing with other problems, a lot more difficult ones, so this was not in the focus of my attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you were called up and told you were part of this special civilian police unit, you reported to a place called Rakovacke Bare in the Banja Luka area; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's where that unit was stationed, that police unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that had previously been a JNA facility; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I really don't know what it was used for.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: A lot of people who had been in the military police with you came over to this civilian police unit together with you; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
