utterances.text: Yes, I saw some of the people who were with me in the military police. I saw them there at the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 07096.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, this will be a report on the activities of the CSB Banja Luka Special Police Detachment. Now, at the bottom of page 1 in the B/C/S, and turning to page 2 in the English, and in the English, we're at the bottom of page 2, we read that in co-operation with the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina army units, the detachment participated in combat, and it refers to the territory of several municipalities, including Bosanski Novi, Prijedor, Sanski Most, and at the end, Kotor Varos. That's right, isn't it, what we read there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely what it is written, just as you read it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the detachment did, in fact, participate in combat in co-operation with the VRS in those municipalities; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out of these municipalities, I just know about the municipality of Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you saw just know about the municipality of Kotor Varos, you mean you were deployed there yourself as a member of this unit; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For a while, for about 15 or 20 days. I'm not sure. 15?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document bearing number 07096 receives number P7159.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7159 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we discussed members of the military police with you who had also come over to the special unit. A number of the members of the Banja Luka Serb Defence Forces, or SOS, also became part of this special unit; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot speak about the people who were joining in there. The people who received call-up papers were there. I don't really understand what it is that you're asking about when you say "Defence Forces."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's have 65 ter 06899.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is Glas from the 29th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in the B/C/S, we're looking for the bottom right part of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in the third paragraph - sorry, fourth - Stojan Zupljanin, the head of CSB Banja Luka, is quoted as saying -- or is described as saying that: "A large number of the fighters of the Serbian Defence Forces, SOS, being reliable and experienced fighters, would be tested for engagement in the special detachment ..." What I'm putting to you is: After those tests, many former SOS members became part of this special detachment of the Banja Luka CSB; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I see what is written here, but who they are and how they came into being, I really cannot say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that you weren't aware what the head of CSB Banja Luka was saying publicly about the unit that you were a member of in 1992?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see we're at or near the time for the break. I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I would have one follow-up question before we take that break. Are you familiar with a unit or a group which was called the SOS, or is it for the first time that you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did hear about the SOS, but I don't know anything about it. It does ring a bell, but I don't know anything about the composition of that unit, who its members were or any such thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From whom did you hear, and when, about the SOS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a notorious fact in the town of Banja Luka. Everybody knew about the existence of the SOS unit. I don't know who that unit belonged to, whether it belonged to the military or the police, I really don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What, then, was common knowledge about the SOS? I mean, what was it that everyone knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew about the existence of the SOS unit. Others did. But whatever else I were to tell you, it would just be my guess-work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But what did you know about -- well, first of all, you said you knew what everyone knew. So there you expressed what everyone apparently knew. But what did you know then about the existence of the SOS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everybody knew about the existence of that unit. I knew it as well. I don't know who they belonged to, so I can't go into that. I knew that there was a unit of that kind in Banja Luka, but I don't know anything about its composition or who they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But was it just -- first of all, I may have misunderstood or misread one of your previous answers when you said "others did," because my follow-up question was ignoring that part of your answer, and I apologise for that. But now what was it -- you knew that there was a unit of "that kind." What kind? Or just under that name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't mention what kind of unit it was. I just said that I knew of it. I didn't know its composition or hierarchy or who they belonged to. I just heard of its existence. I knew that they existed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I referred to the answer which was translated to us as: "I knew that there was a unit of that kind in Banja Luka ..." So if I understand you well, the talk of the town was SOS exists. What was the reputation, what was -- what was said about it, apart from that it exists?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know much about that unit. It existed, and that's all I knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say, "I didn't know much about that unit." But it's just that you say, Well, SOS exists. That's -- is that a subject of conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's very hard for me to answer that question after such a long time. I can only say that I was aware of its existence, of the existence of some such unit. However, after such a long time, I really can't tell you what the talk of the town was in 1992. It was such a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take the break, but, Mr. Traldi, anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Might I very briefly follow up?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, very briefly then. Because we are really at the time of the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, the Chamber has received evidence that among their other activities, the SOS was responsible for blockading Banja Luka at the beginning of April. Now, that was, in fact, one of the actions that made them notorious, as you described, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that they were notorious, that the unit was notorious.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll maintain my request to tender the document and may have further questions about that unit after the break, but I won't press any further now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document 06899 receives number P7160.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7160 is admitted. We take break and we'll resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But not until after the witness has left the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom. Meanwhile, the Chamber informs the parties that this Wednesday, at the first break, the Tribunal's photographer will take a panoramic photograph while the court is in session. This photograph will be used on the Tribunal's "Legacy" web site, and the parties had been previously informed about this through an informal communication. The taking of the photograph will not exceed two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you may proceed; however, the Chamber noted that the word "notorious" was not unambiguous in its meaning. Notorious facts do not need to be proven, but the Chamber gained the impression that you used the word in a way different from what the witness did. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Could we have 65 ter 06978.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a list of members of the Banja Luka -- it says SCB in the English, Special Police Detachment. The payroll for August 1992. At number 1 we see Mirko Lukic. He was the commander; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And then Ljuban Ecim and Zdravko Samardzija, they were also part of the unit's leadership; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They were the deputies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you're aware that Mr. Ecim had been involved with the Banja Luka SOS?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know Mr. Ecim personally, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 5 in both languages --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the previous answer is not an answer to the question. The fact was whether you knew that he was involved in the Banja Luka SOS. Even if you don't know him personally, you may have knowledge about that. Did you have that kind of knowledge or did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't know that, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Here at number 102, we see your name, the amount you were paid, and your signature. Is it correct that as of August 1992, you were still being paid by the Banja Luka CSB for service in the special unit?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was my regular salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document 06978 receives number P7161.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 07005, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a document dated the 14th of August, 1992, sent from CSB Banja Luka to subordinate SJBs. It's actually listed as the chief of all SJBs. The command of the 1st Krajina Corps, the chief of the intelligence security organ thereof, and it refers to an order by the Presidency of the Serbian Republic and then says it's implementing that by disbanding the special police detachment and says in the second paragraph: "The troops and materiel are to be reattached to the commander of the 1st Krajina Corps of the Serbian Republic as of the above date." Now it was this order on the basis of which you and other members of the special unit were reattached to the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document 07005 receives number P7162.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32129. Could we turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So we see here an order from Stojan Zupljanin dated the 31st of December, 1992, and it appoints Mr. Ecim and Mr. Samardzija, who you confirmed earlier were part of the leadership of the special detachment when you were in it, to positions in the CSB's police brigade. So it's right that some of the members of the special unit, including some of the leaders, remained in the service of the Banja Luka CSB after the order we just saw; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this arises from this document, it seems to be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd tender the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document 32129 receives number P7163.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to turn now to your deployment to Kotor Varos as a member of the special unit. About how many members of your unit were deployed there with you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were deployed in two teams. I went with the second team. I believe that some 20 of us were deployed on that occasion, and I don't know how many people were deployed with the first team.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Who told you to go to Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mirko Lukic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember who told me to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you went -- both of those teams that you're referring to went to Kotor Varos in June of 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose so. I suppose it was June.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And while you were in Kotor Varos, you were accommodated in a house that was between the Kotor Varos police station and the health centre; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32135. Your Honours, just to explain, it's a large file, which is why it's taking a moment to load. As soon I provide the explanation, it became unnecessary, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this is an aerial image of the part of Kotor Varos we've just discussed taken after the war. Do you see the Kotor Varos SJB on this image?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, indeed, an aerial image, so it's very difficult for me to get my bearings. I know where the SJB in Kotor Varos is, but as I'm looking at this image ... could you perhaps assist me?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If you look at the lower part of the building -- or the image, rather, and perhaps start with the building with a number of cars in the parking lot, look at that area, and see if it assists you in identifying the SJB.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If you just take a moment and then tell us if, in that area, you're able to identify one of those buildings as the police station.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know where the police station is. I'm confused by this aerial image, however. I'm finding it very difficult. I can't identify it, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Are you able to recognise the health centre, or the area where it was?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the football pitch, but for the rest of it, I really can't, I'm sorry. I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I won't insist further.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we can take this off the screen, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You mentioned you were between the health centre and the SJB. About how far were you, the house were accommodated in, from the health centre?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 300 metres, approximately, from the gate of the health centre to the house; 300 metres approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And about how far from the SJB?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the house was halfway between the health centre and the SJB. Halfway. It's very hard for me to give you the exact distance, not in metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the command of your unit was based in the SJB at the time; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, of course, you got your orders from the command of the unit during your deployment in Kotor Varos; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the commanders who had been appointed to those positions there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Which one gave you your orders while you were deployed in Kotor Varos? Which commander?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the name. We were attached to a unit or whoever. We were just attached to that unit, so I can't remember any names. I already said that to your investigators when they interviewed me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you know part of your unit was also accommodated in a sawmill in Kotor Varos during that time; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the direction of the sawmill. I never went there. There was a facility which was previously a shoe factory or some such thing. I never went there. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The sawmill we're talking about is the Pilana sawmill; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go there. Because there was a danger of sniper fire, and we were suggested not to pass through that open space.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart now to show a few clips from a video which have collectively been given 65 ter 32131a. And for two of the four clips, we won't be relying on the audio so those we'll only play once. They're all quite brief. And for the first one, I say for her benefit, if we could play from the beginning to 3.2 seconds or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'd asked for here, sir, to ask: Do you recognise the man in glasses that we see at the forefront of the image?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the green camouflage uniforms and red berets that we see on these men, that's the uniform your unit wore during its deployment in Kotor Varos; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. We had all sorts of uniforms. We were pretty much left to our own devices to obtain our uniforms, so there were all sorts of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's play forward to 6.7 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going test your evidence on that in a moment, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And do you recognise this man?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not very clear. The image is not very clear. Can you rewind just a little and can you replay it from there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I really can't say, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recognise the patch he's wearing?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a patch on his left-side pocket, something red and white but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in your interview that you testified was truthful, you suggested this was a patch your unit had gotten when it went to Vecici, in Kotor Varos, during your deployment there. Does that refresh your recollection as to that patch?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said something else. Those were daily markings that the troops wore in order to be recognised on that particular day. They changed daily. One day they were white; the other they were blue. So it was not a permanent patch or a permanent marking.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is one of those patches that your unit received during its deployment in Kotor Varos, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Then I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to play the second clip and stop at 10 seconds. This one we will have to play twice for the audio but the audio doesn't relate to the first ten seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Actually, we can stop there. And for the record, that's at 4.9 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, the blue APC that we see in the centre here, that is an armoured personnel carrier that your unit had and used during its deployment in Kotor Varos; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a MUP APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you can tell it's a MUP APC because it's been painted blue; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recognise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The question was also: Was this vehicle attached to your unit and did your unit use it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I used to see it up there. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You saw it. But was it used by your unit? That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recognise the white building in the distance?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart now to play the rest of the clip and then we'll play it the second time for the audio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It having been played for the second time, I would expect interpretation, but I didn't hear anything. Could we play it again? You have provided the booth with --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I haven't, but I'm told we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could we play it again and then receive translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Stand right there, hands, three fingers. Three fingers. Three. Three. That's right."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, first, that's the Kotor Varos SJB that those three men were in at the end of the image, right -- the end of the video?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot -- I cannot confirm whether that's that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You don't recognise the building where your unit's command was headquartered during your deployment?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I never entered that building while I was there; and secondly, from here, nothing can be recognised. Everything is similar, all the buildings are similar. But I did not enter the police building while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We saw that the man who was being put up against the wall was told "three fingers" on each side. That's a Serbian salute, three fingers; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbs do have this three-finger salute, but I don't see what this has to do with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The only thing you have to do is answer the questions. You don't have to wonder what the one has to do with the other. That's for the parties and for the Chamber to further consider. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to play the third clip, the first six seconds only. This one we won't be relying on any audio.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, do you recognise this man?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And who's this?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is Nenad Stevandic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see he's wearing the same as we saw on the gentleman earlier, green camouflage, red beret, and the patch that was among the patches issued to your unit; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This picture is quite clear so this can be discerned, as opposed to the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart -- we've stopped at 6.6 seconds to be totally precise. I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to play the rest of the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, he is about to walk over to two other men. At the end of the video, I'll ask whether you also recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you recognise the two men Mr. Stevandic had walked over to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognised one of them. It's Mr. Ljuban Ecim on the left. I don't know about the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In the interview, you suggested the other was Nenad Kajkut. Would it refresh your recollection if I suggested that that's, in fact, who the other man is?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you were to replay this film again, maybe I could, because, right now, I really couldn't tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we're starting at 20 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The right-hand side, that should be Nenad Kajkut. I can tell by the moustache, although it's rather difficult to tell here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have the fourth clip now. And this one we'll have to play twice.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "You want me to open it for you. "Huh. "Open this shit. "Let me go to get the keys. "Open it. "I didn't bring the keys. "Open this shit, you fucker. You'll open it now. "Okay, okay, okay. "Crowbar, open it with a crowbar."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The two men in uniform were again wearing green camouflage, red berets, and the same patch we had seen in the previous clips; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You testified there were 20 men deployed with you. Did you recognise the people in your unit's uniforms in this clip?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember. These are universal uniforms, the ones that we saw a moment ago. I did not have such a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You said these are universal uniforms. You testified a moment ago that the patch was part of daily patches specifically given to members of your unit so they could distinguish each other from people who weren't in the unit. So it wouldn't work to use something universal for that, would it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Insignia changed daily, but not uniforms. Insignia, not uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you recognise the two men in that video that we saw shoving and kicking the man in the T-shirt and jeans? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know these men.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender that video. I believe all four clips are 65 ter 32131a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, they would receive number P7164.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7164 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, at one point during your time in Kotor Varos, you were deployed to the village of Vrbanjci; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were in Kotor Varos.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, could we have 65 ter 32097.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is your OTP interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And let's start on page 65. The way the transcript is, it's in both English and B/C/S, so it's one document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So at the bottom here, you're asked, beginning at line 30: "Was -- Vrbanjci is a Muslim village?" And turning to the next page, you say: "I think it is. It's possible." You're asked: "Was there -- what time of day was this that you were there?" And you answer: "It was day-time." And then you're asked some more questions but I'm going to stop there. It's true that you were deployed to Vrbanjci during your time in Kotor Varos as a member of the special unit; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were there one day, and I said that in my statement. Otherwise I was deployed in Kotor Varos, and we talked about that a moment ago, about that house where we were. So we were there for one day, and that is contained in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, may I take you back. You were asked: "Now at one point during your time in Kotor Varos, you were deployed to the village of Vrbanjci; right." You said: "No, we were in Kotor Varos." That answer therefore was not accurate. Because for one day, at one point in time during your stay in Kotor Varos you were in Vrbanjci.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not understand the question. At one point in time, that's what I didn't understand, the context of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But at one point in time during your time in Kotor Varos, didn't you understand that that was at a moment when you were in Kotor Varos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't understand that the question referred to a moment. I didn't understand that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You didn't understand the question. Then next time, instead of answering it, ask for clarification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you learned after the war about crimes that were committed against the population of Vrbanjci, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What crimes against that village did you learn about specifically?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically through conversations and talks with the other side concerning missing persons and exchanges, we discussed the requests that were put to us, that is to say, through this work that we dealt with later.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you've answered a different question than the one I asked. I hadn't asked about the mechanics of how you learned about it. I asked: What do you know, as you sit there today, was done to the people who lived in the village of Vrbanjci?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What happened? I don't know anything, but I know that a large number of missing persons are still being searched for. But what it was that happened over there, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: People who have been missing since 1992.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are missing persons. I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you're also aware that during your deployment in Kotor Varos, while you were living between the police station and the health centre, dozens of people were killed, Muslims were killed, at and near the health centre in Kotor Varos; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. And I said that in my statement, that I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You've never heard in the course of your work and you never heard at that time in 1992 of a mass murder committed just a couple of hundred metres from where you were living?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If I could have just one second, Your Honours. I apologise. Could we have P3711.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an extract of the minutes of the 40th Session of the Crisis Staff held at 0800 hours on 26th of June, 1992, in Kotor Varos. And if we look to the bottom of the page in both languages where there's a reference to Nedjo Djukanovic, right before that we read: "Dr. Gajanin informed the Crisis Staff of the situation as regards casualties and reported on what had been done on the premises of the health centre by members of the special unit, which he had tried to prevent, but was driven away at gunpoint." And then Mr. Djekanovic says he is told someone named Dubocanin, about everything going on in the town and at the health centre, and that information would be provided on the behaviour of the members of the special unit at the meeting with S. Zupljanin, the chief of the CSB, scheduled for the next day. Now, first, very specific question: This meeting, 26 June 1992, this was during the time that you were in Kotor Varos; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was in Kotor Varos during that period. But I did not attend this session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were there with just a couple of dozen other members of the special unit, the Crisis Staff knew about it, Dubocanin knew about it. Is it really your evidence that you had no idea that members of your relatively small unit had committed mass murder quite close to the home where you were staying?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, first of all, I came later with 20 men, and up there there were already almost 100 men. I said that I came with a group later, with 20 men. Secondly, I came some seven or ten days after the first group, and I stayed there for up to 15 days, maximum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I ask you, was that the first group, the 100 men you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe I didn't understand that question. The first group consisting of 100 men went to Kotor Varos, and we went seven or ten days later, this group consisting of 20 persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just -- one second. If you give me one second. Yes, I read one of your previous answers: "I went with the second team. I believe it was some 20 of us were deployed on that occasion, and I don't know how many people were deployed with the first team." So apparently within half an hour, now you suddenly remember that there were 100 approximately. Any explanation for not knowing it earlier and now suddenly telling us that these 100 men were the first group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said around 100, perhaps more, perhaps less. I did not say precisely how many.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe it could have been more, maybe it could have been less, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But your previous answer was: "And I don't know how many people were deployed with the first team." But you knew it because it was around 100. Any explanation as to why you didn't tell us at the time how big -- how large that group was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I'm not sure even now how many men there were there. Around 100. Perhaps more, perhaps less. However, it's very hard to be precise. And you're asking me for precision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking for precision. I'm asking for an explanation between you telling us that you didn't know how much the first group was, where for the second group you said "some 20," so for the first group, you could have said -- you could have expressed yourself in similar terms, "around," or "some." And then half an hour later, you know that it was approximately 100. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You are aware, aren't you, as you sit there today, that members of your unit were involved in committing crimes against non-Serbs in Kotor Varos during your deployment there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. And I know that that unit did not commit any crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm done with this topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you clarify the last answer, you know that they did not commit any crimes. What -- how are you so pertinent in telling us that you know apparently for sure that they did not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The crimes that were committed in Kotor Varos were committed by some other units, the so-called unit Burce or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what's the source of knowledge for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Source of knowledge are post-war sources of knowledge through the work that I am doing now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you be a bit more precise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that there was this group called Burce, or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Again not an answer to my question, how do you know that. But, second, how do you know that they were the ones who slaughtered these persons or killed them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know because I am working on missing persons and I took part in the exhumations, all the exhumations in Kotor Varos, with the prosecutor's office and all other teams from Zenica, and I learned about all of this, and that is what I'm testifying about here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But from an exhumation, you wouldn't know who killed those who are exhumed, would you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not from the exhumations but from conversations with the investigative organs that were working on this. I knew that because judges, the police, are all in attendance and that is the situation when such questions are being discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there are any reports which would further support the evidence of the witness in this respect, Mr. Lukic and Mr. Traldi, of course, the Chamber would always like to have an opportunity to -- to find corroboration of what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll certainly check, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Before we do, sir, which crimes specifically in Kotor Varos municipality were you told that the Burce unit committed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it has to do with Vrbanjci and Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you're describing what you know to be massacres; yes?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never mentioned any massacres. I just said that I draw my knowledge from the investigative organs that were carrying out investigations in the post-war period because I was involved, together with these investigative organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you learned from them at exhumations. Exhumations are related to people who have been killed, not homes that have been looted, right? These are about people -- these crimes that you referring to, these are about murder; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have just been speaking about missing persons, not looted homes. I think that I was clear enough. During exhumations, the appropriate institutions are in attendance and they're carrying out investigations and it is only natural about the perpetrators of such crimes. Precisely when talking to investigative organs who were carrying out these investigations and that was the team in Zenica, that is to say, the court, the prosecutor's office, and the police from Zenica, when speaking to them, I learned about these details that I'm testifying about here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Burce unit, did they also tell you who its commander was?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I ask a question before this page disappears. Give me a moment. You were -- at page 71, line 21, Mr. Traldi asked you: "Sir, which crimes specifically in Kotor Varos municipality were you told that the Burce unit committed?" You said: "Well, I think it has to do with Vrbanjci and Grabovica." Now, I think you said Vrbanjci and Grabovica are areas of -- names of places. The question was what crimes? Which crimes were committed? Do you think you can answer that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I've already said it's the locations where they were committed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Now I have the following question for you. You said you know for sure that your unit did not commit those crimes, that is, killing persons in Vrbanjci, a larger number of persons. Asked you how do you know? You said, I know because the Burce group committed those crimes. And now asked about it, what do you know about crimes committed by the Burce unit, you say, Well, I know of locations but not about crimes, which makes your reliance on the Burce group committing crimes in Vrbanjci not very strong because you say you do not know what crimes they, that is, the Burce group, had committed. Any comment on this analysis of your logic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do have a comment. Because the unit, the special forces of MUP, they did not go into such actions. Secondly, as far as Vrbanjci is concerned, I said that crimes were committed, that I know that and I draw that knowledge from my post-war work. And I will repeat once again, investigative organs mentioned this Burce unit that committed these crimes in that particular place. What the specific crimes were, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But nevertheless you insist that it was the Burce unit who would have committed those killings and at the same time you're telling us that you don't know what crimes they did commit. That -- I have some difficulties in reconciling the two.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no doubt that a crime was committed in Grabovica. There's no doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. We started the whole thing with Vrbanjci. You added Grabovica to it. We did not. So let's focus on Vrbanjci and not move away to Grabovica at this moment. Please proceed, continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've just been testifying on that topic, the knowledge I acquired in the post-war period from the investigative organs that were carrying out this investigation, and I know that they mentioned this group Burce. That is what I have been talking about. I don't know what happened during the course of the war. I don't have any knowledge about that. What I know is what I have been testifying about here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to try one more time. What they told you about what the Burce group did in Vrbanjci was that that group killed people; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that they killed people. I'm going to repeat from the umpteenth time: I found out from the investigative organs that were carrying out the investigation up there that a crime had been committed there and the group of Burce has been mentioned. I don't know anything more about that group. I don't know who the commander is, where they come from. There was only mention of this group called Burce.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So I want to make sure I understand the conversation you had that you're recounting to us now. Somebody told you in Vrbanjci the Burce group committed a crime, and you didn't say, What kind of crime? Or what were the consequences of it? Or in relation to your professional work, have the victims ever been found? You didn't ask any of those questions. The topic was simply dropped and you started talking about something else. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not depart from the topic. Investigative actions are carried out by others, the police the judiciary, the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop --

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is their mandate and their job.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No one has asked you about whose mandate this is. What you've been asked is: Did you simply drop the topic? You said no. Okay? You were told a crime had been committed in Burce -- or by the Burce unit in Vrbanjci. The conversation didn't end there, as you've just told us. What else did you learn about that crime?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not learn anything else. I told you what I learned and how I learned it, and now you are pushing the topic further, asking me to give you an answer to a question that I simply cannot answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If I could have just one question to complete this before the break, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You'd also said, in your view, there was no doubt that a crime had been committed in Grabovica. That was a mass murder, and you know from your professional work that for almost all the victims, their bodies have never been found; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bodies have never been found. But I didn't say that. I said there is no doubt about the fact that a crime had been committed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will turn to a new topic after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then again, the same question. A crime. What crime? Theft?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, a large number of people in Grabovica are still considered missing. Through my -- our work, so far -- please, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, no. You said no doubt that a crime has been committed. Which crime you say there's no doubt about that had been committed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A crime against the people missing from Grabovica who have not been found to this very day. Very few bones were found in Majdan. I was there together with the investigative teams. And those remains were later identified by DNA analysis, and it was established that the bones belonged to the persons who had gone missing from Kotor Varos municipality, i.e., from Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's still not a crime, is it? If someone went missing, it's not a crime. What crime, therefore, you said there was no doubt that had been committed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't intend to justify any crime if a -- somebody's death was violent --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking you whether you intend to justify anything. I'm putting a simple question to you. And again and again, and it's not the first time, you are going around the question and you do not answer the question. We'll take a break, and we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher. Mr. Traldi, any idea about the time you'd still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd say I'm slightly ahead of my estimate but not by very much, and I don't expect in practical terms to finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I must say that I don't have your estimate clearly on my mind at this very moment, but you certainly will assist me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: My estimate had been two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two and a half hours. That was -- yes, was increased. We'll take a break, and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom, Mr. Lukic and Mr. Mladic, even when the Court has not yet entered the courtroom, you should refrain from addressing the public gallery or to seek communications with them. It has been told several times to you now. You apparently ignore it again. Mr. Mladic, you are just continuing to do it. Would you please turn. Otherwise -- otherwise you'll be removed from the courtroom. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to turn now to your evidence about the exchange commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now can we have 65 ter 32128.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this is a document coming from Colonel Gojko Vujinovic, the 1st Krajina Corps assistant commander for civilian affairs. And it's dated the 30th of September, 1994. First we see it's titled: "Exchange of civilian population." Does that refresh your recollection as to whether civilians were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Within the context of exchanges, just as I told you a little while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. And what we see here in the first paragraph is a reference to the state commission agreeing on an exchange of civilians, Muslims from Sanski Most for Serbs from Bugojno. Three buses arriving from Sanski Most and then a description of the timing of the exchange. And then below that it says: "The unit command carry out the necessary tasks to ensure that this is carried out." So VRS units in the area where exchanges of civilians took place had tasks to carry out to facilitate those exchanges; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Conditions had to be put in place for the passage of the buses through the separation line. In other words, fire had to be discontinued for the buses to go either way. And that includes the buses coming from Bugojno as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 32128.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document receives number P7165.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn to the exchanges you took direct part in and I want to ask about some of the process of organising one. I'm going to ask specific questions. When you would receive -- your exchange commission would receive a list of soldiers that the ABiH or the HVO was looking for, you would turn that list over to a member of the exchange commission who was part of the 1st Krajina Corps' security organ; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was a member of the commission for exchanges of the 1st Krajina Corps. We would forward those lists to the corps command, seeking an answer to the question as to what had happened to the people who were on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, specifically the way that would work is that the security organ's representative on the exchange commission would forward it up his chain of command; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the security organ, the corps command, and, if necessary, to the Main Staff. It all depended on the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So who was the representative on the exchange commission from the 1st Krajina Corps' security organ? What was his name?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several people as needed. One of them was Colonel Uros Mirosljevic [phoen] and then Vladimir Sevarika [phoen]. There was another gentleman whose name I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the commission also included representatives of other organs of the corps command; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The commission consisted of commission members and the representative of the security organs who monitored the work of the commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Was there ever a representative from the religious, morale, and legal affairs organ, to whom you've testified the commission was subordinated?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were under the authority of that organ, but nobody from that organ was a member of our commission. We were subordinated to them or, rather, our work was supervised along the line of profession by them. But that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you say in your statement that you'd receive approvals for your work by the VRS Main Staff through the corps command. Who in the Main Staff would issue such approvals?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the type of approval that was needed. For example, if fire had to be discontinued during negotiations, then we would receive approval from the corps command. There was no need for the Main Staff to be involved. And if it was about an exchange of prisoners of war, then we would get in touch with the Main Staff. That was the procedure we followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you haven't answered my original question. Who on the Main Staff would you get in touch with to receive an approval for such an exchange?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did answer. We would get in touch with the corps command, and the corps command, in its turn, would address the Main Staff for approval. We got in touch with the corps command, and then the corps command would address the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you know - yes or no - who in the Main Staff would issue the approval for an exchange?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commission who had issued the application through the corps commander. Again, that was not done directly --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- not directly from them to us. I don't know if you understood me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I note that you're not answering my question. I'm going to try to put it again very simply. You say the Main Staff issued approvals for your work. A moment ago, you say the Main Staff issued approvals for the exchange of prisoners. The Main Staff was comprised of people. When the Main Staff issued a document, one of these people's names would appear at the bottom. When the Main Staff issued an approval for the exchange of prisoners, which of those people's names would appear at the bottom, if you know?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two names appeared. A naval captain whose name I really don't know. And Colonel Tolimir was the other. I believe that there was another person who approved those things, but I can't remember his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Was the captain Mr. Beara?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't remember the name of the person whose rank was naval captain. That was his rank but I can't remember the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 01062.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, as it comes up, though you didn't mention him a moment ago, General Mladic had the authority to issue orders about the functioning of the corps's exchange commission; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that. I know that our authority reached up to the corps command. I don't want to go into the authorities and competencies of General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're a soldier in the army. Your evidence is that you don't know whether the chief of the Main Staff had the authority to issue an order about your work; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I didn't know. I didn't see any such document. Therefore, I can't talk about that. I don't have any doubts about that. But I don't know. I was a member of the corps commission, and there were six other commissions on top of that. All the commissions operated with the Main Staff through their commands, and they sought approval for their work from the Main Staff. I was not on the level of the Main Staff. Therefore, I can't testify about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's see if we can refresh your recollection. This is a document coming from the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. It's dated the 5th of January, 1993. It's titled: "Instructions regarding the exchange of prisoners of war."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the English it's the singular not the plural, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise. I misspoken, Mr. President. It is the singular, "instruction."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see some paragraphs of text. Below that, we see it's directing that a set of instructions be adhered to, including the forming of commissions for the exchange of prisoners of war in the corps commands; and, at point 3, using a computer to process the records of captured, missing and killed soldiers at the corps level.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to the end of the document in both languages. In the English, we see we've got the very last page that this is sent to the commands of the various corps. And if we turn a page back in the English only, we'll see that this is type signed by General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, does this refresh your recollection as to whether General Mladic had the authority to issue, in this case, what's labelled an instruction on the functioning of the corps-level exchange commissions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a typed name of General Ratko Mladic. I already stated that we received our instructions from the Main Staff. This is just one of the instructions which was issued in January 1993, whereas I joined the commission in April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender 65 ter 01062.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 01062 receives number P7166.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we turn briefly back to the first page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see -- for the moment, I'm simple directing your attention to the confidential number on it, 31/15-20/93.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now could we have 65 ter 32106.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see here a document coming from the 1st Krajina Corps Command dated the 18th of May, 1993, issued pursuant to order confidential number 31/15-20/93. Now, I have a couple of questions for you about this document. The first question I have is: At the end of this first paragraph, we see that General Talic writes: "We are authorised to exchange prisoners of war and bodily remains and help in organising the exchange of civilians and art and church valuables." So it's clear from this document that the 1st Krajina Corps understood itself to be authorised to assist in the exchange of the civilians; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But only with assisting and not in implementing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Second, we see a list of nine persons being appointed and we see this is dated the 18th of May, 1993. We don't see your name. Do you recall when you were appointed and whether it was as part of a different decision? Sorry, we have eight names in the original.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, in the month of April 1993, I joined the commission, and I spent perhaps three or four months being there, learning about the way of work of the commission and its purview in order to be able to negotiate with the other side. My name is not here because I was still not appointed as a person who could work and negotiate on behalf of the commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's been pointed out to me there's a difference in the last name in the B/C/S and the English and so I'm done with the document. I'll ask that it be marked for identification at this moment and we'll look into that matter further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that in English a name is added.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It does. This is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are nine names in English and there are eight in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. And I apologise for not looking into it earlier, but I'd simply ask that the document be marked and we'll look into it now. Or shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document to be MFI'd unless Judge Fluegge would have an -- no. Please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 32106 will receive number P7167.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It should be 7167.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's now clearly on the screen. Is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The problem, Mr. Traldi, in my view, is that there's a name under item 9 added. That can't be just be a translation error. Where does it come from if the original doesn't contain this name?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that what's I'd intended to say we would look into, Your Honour. I admit I had focused on other aspects of the document in my preparation but I'm not tendering it at the moment. And we'll report back to the Chamber when we've got something to report, as it were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll hear from you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P6914.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we saw General Mladic's order or General Mladic's instruction a moment ago referred to maintaining computerised records of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is the number again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Will you please say it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: 6914. And if we could have page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a document coming from the Republika Srpska Exchange Commission. If we look under the second name, Mihrudin Begovic, we see the description according to information received from the 1st Krajina Corps Exchange Commission from their computer, on 14/05/1993. Now, first, it's correct, isn't it, that the 1st Krajina Corps maintained computerised records of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the scope of the technical capabilities that existed at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see after that information there's a person from Civcije. That's in Doboj municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Civcije is near Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that this person was transferred to another prison on 13th of December, 1992. We see a reference to a list of persons captured from Manjaca held on -- held in KP Dom Butmir. So the 1st Krajina Corps' computerised records reflected that people were transferred, for instance, from Manjaca to KP Dom Butmir through the network of Republika Srpska detention facilities; right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see it from this document. However, the date of the document precedes the time when I was appointed as a commission member, so it would be very hard for me to say anything else about this document and what I know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to ask only now about these computerised records. Who entered information in those records?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: A colleague of ours, Mrs. Mirjana Mira Jokanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now did she just type in whatever came to mind or find information herself, or did somebody tell her what information to enter?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose that somebody must have told her what to type, i.e., provided her with information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you would provide her with information about prisoners the 1st Krajina Corps was holding which she would then enter into these records; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The computer database which was created in 1994 was primarily relative to the persons who went missing and who were on the lists of Republika Srpska. Also certain documents were entered if the president of the commission deemed it necessary for them to be entered into the computer database.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, here it's clear that this information is being reflected as being provided from the computer in May of 1993. In fact, these records existed no later than the 14th of May, 1993, as we see here; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could zoom in on the middle of the page in the B/C/S to assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, these are computer entries. In 1993 we still had problems with technology and it was really an issue as to what could be entered into a computer database, bearing in mind the development of the computer technology and how well versed people were to use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, we see this is a person who it says was transferred to another prison as of the 13th of December, 1992. That means, I would put to you, that means transferred from Manjaca to either, as a first step, either Batkovici or Kula, but outside of the 1st Krajina Corps' area of responsibility. So my question to you is: Did the 1st Krajina Corps already have computerised records of prisoners in 1992, or did it later, when those records were created, add information about people who had been added in 1992 in its area of responsibility on the basis of other records? If you know.

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot speak about 1992 because, really, I wasn't there. As can be seen from my statement, from April 1993 I was on the commission. And you're asking about 1992, and I was not there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the answer is you do not know. That's the simple answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because the last three words of the question were "if you know." You don't know. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32101.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'll be continuing to discuss recording information about prisoners although in a slightly different regard. Now, we see -- and here it refers to captured enemy soldiers. We see in this document coming from the Command of the 1st Krajina Corps' Intelligence and Security Department a reference to a letter from the Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners of War. Refers to a number of prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we turn to page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And towards the bottom of the B/C/S, below the four names, we read: "We also need to ensure that the ICRC registers all the enemy prisoners in our prisons, apart from those, of course, who are of special interest to us or have committed war crimes against the civilian population and our prisoners." And we see it's type signed by Colonel Stevan Bogojevic. Now, you were aware that it was the position of the 1st Krajina Corps's security and intelligence organ that the ICRC should be allowed to register prisoners except for some prisoners who are of special interest to the security and intelligence organ or prisoners it believed to have committed crimes?

utterances.speaker: GORAN KRCMAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew of the position that in prisons, all POWs should be registered. This is a document of the security organs that was not available to me, and I was not aware of this other paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document as the next public Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 32101 receives number P7168.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Mr. Traldi, I'm looking at the clock. We have 90 seconds left.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I was too, Mr. President, and today I think I'll be cautious and suggest that perhaps we break 90 seconds earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krcmar, we adjourn for the day. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in the morning, tomorrow morning when we'll conclude your evidence -- we'll conclude hearing your evidence. I again instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever it is about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given. If that is clear to you, you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 3rd of March, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 3rd day of March, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.
